claim: For every differentiable unital qubit evolution whose Bloch vector obeys \(\dot x(t)=D(t)x(t)\), and every full-rank Bloch state \(x\in\mathbb R^3\) with \(\|x\|<1\), put \(\bar D=D+D^{\mathsf T}\) and \(R_x=I+xx^{\mathsf T}/(1-\|x\|^2)\). The infinitesimal Bures/Fisher growth matrix \(J_B\) used by Hall, Cresser, Li, and Andersson satisfies \[4J_B=R_x\bar D R_x.\] Since \(R_x\) is positive definite and invertible, \(J_B\) and \(\bar D\) have exactly the same inertia. Consequently, at every time and every full-rank state, the infinitesimal Bures/Fisher witness has a positive growth direction if and only if the trace-distance witness does, equivalently if and only if \(\lambda_{\max}(D+D^{\mathsf T})>0\). For the Hall--Cresser--Li--Andersson example \(D(t)=\operatorname{diag}(-1+\tanh t,-1+\tanh t,-2)\), this proves analytically that \(J_B\) is negative definite for every finite \(t\ge0\), replacing the numerical check in the source. The claim concerns the local infinitesimal Bures/Fisher witness on full-rank states; it does not assert equality of integrated non-Markovianity measures or equality of finite-separation distance trajectories.
integrity: The theorem is proved by an exact rank-one matrix factorization and Sylvester congruence. The bundled checker is a finite algebraic consistency test only and is not used as proof of the universal statement. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The statement is for differentiable unital qubit dynamics and the local infinitesimal Bures/Fisher metric on full-rank states. It does not equate integrated non-Markovianity measures or finite-separation distance trajectories, and it does not cover non-unital translation terms.
title: Bures and trace-distance local witnesses have identical inertia for unital qubit dynamics
